column2: 中古英语 stampen（捣、砸）← 古英语 stempan（捣碎）← 原始日耳曼语 *stampōną（踩踏、击打）← 原始印欧语 *stemb-（踏下去）
column3: a small piece of paper stuck on mail to show that postage has been paid
column5: He stuck a stamp on the envelope.|She stamped her foot in anger.
column6: a hard press downward that leaves a mark – 重重压下去、留下印记
column7: 邮票：盖过戳才算付过邮资，那一小片纸因此得名|图章：压下去留印的那件工具|踩踏：脚重重压向地面，还是同一个动作

column2: 英语 standard ← 古法语 estandart（集合地、军旗）← 法兰克语 *standahard（站得稳）
column3: agreed as the usual level or quality that others are measured against
column5: This is standard practice in most hospitals.|The room comes with standard equipment.
column6: taken as the fixed measure everyone is held to – 拿来当尺度、人人照它比的那一档
column7: 标准的：符合公认那一档的|标准：那把公认的尺度本身|规格：把尺度落到具体数值与形制上

column2: 由 stand ＋ point 复合而成，仿译德语 Standpunkt（站立点）
column3: the position from which someone looks at a matter
column5: From a legal standpoint, the contract is void.|Consider it from the buyer's standpoint.
column6: the spot you stand on that decides what you see – 你所站的那一处，决定你看见什么
column7: 立场：人所站的位置，引申为所持的态度|观点：从那个位置看出去所得的看法

column2: 中古英语 stapel ← 古英语 stapol（柱、桩）← 原始日耳曼语 *stapulaz（柱）；「大宗商品」义另出一支，经古法语 estaple（集市）与晚期拉丁语 stapula 传入，与此同源
column3: a small u-shaped metal fastener pushed through paper and bent flat behind
column5: The report was held together by two staples.|Rice is a staple in much of Asia.
column6: the piece that pins things together, or the one good a place lives on – 把东西钉住的那件，或一地赖以为生的那一宗
column7: 订书钉：穿过纸再弯折，把纸扣在一起|主要产品：一地贸易所倚的大宗，如同支住局面的那根柱|主食：饮食里当主的那一宗，同一层意思落到吃上

column2: 中古英语 sterre ← 古英语 steorra ← 原始日耳曼语 *sternô ← 原始印欧语 *h₂stḗr（星）
column3: a huge ball of burning gas that appears as a point of light in the night sky
column5: Thousands of stars appeared once the clouds cleared.|She became a film star at nineteen.
column6: a self-shining point that stands out in the dark – 自身发光、在暗处格外显眼的一点
column7: 恒星：天上自身发光的那类天体|明星：人群里最显眼的那个，借光亮作比|星形：照那一点的画法画成的五角形

column2: 中古英语 staren ← 古英语 starian（凝视）← 原始日耳曼语 *starjaną（僵住、发直）← 原始印欧语 *ster-（硬、僵）
column3: to look at something for a long time without moving the eyes
column5: He stared at the screen without blinking.|Passers-by stared at her bright hat.
column6: to hold the gaze pinned on one thing – 把目光钉在一处不移开
column7: 凝视：目光定住，久看一处|瞪视：同样定住，但带着不满或敌意|注视不动：强调眼珠几乎不转这一点

column2: 中古英语 sterten（猛然跃起、冲出）← 古英语 styrtan（跳起）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sturtijan（使惊动）← 原始印欧语 *(s)ter-（僵、硬）
column3: the point or moment at which something begins
column5: The race had a false start.|He woke with a start at midnight.
column6: the sudden move out of standing still – 从静止里猛然动起来的那一下
column7: 开始：事情由不动转为动的那一刻|出发点：动起来的那个位置|惊跳：受惊时身子猛一动，本义正在这一跳上

column2: 中古英语 startlen（急奔、绊跌）← 古英语 steartlian（踢腾、挣动），即 start ＋ 反复体后缀 -le
column3: to make someone move or jump suddenly from surprise
column5: A loud bang startled the sleeping dog.|Sorry, I did not mean to startle you.
column6: to give someone a jolt that makes the body move – 惊得对方身子猛动一下
column7: 惊动：使人受惊而有所动作|使吓一跳：强调那一下突然且短促

column2: 中古英语 sterven（死去）← 古英语 steorfan（死）← 原始日耳曼语 *sterbaną（僵住而死）← 原始印欧语 *(s)terp-（失力、发麻）；后专指因断粮而死
column3: to suffer or die from having no food
column5: Thousands starved during the long drought.|The plants were starved of light.
column6: to be worn down toward death by having nothing to eat – 因无可吃而一步步耗下去
column7: 饿死：耗到尽头那一步|挨饿：还在耗着、尚未到尽头|极度缺乏：把断粮推广到断任何必需之物

column2: 中古英语 stedy，或续古英语 stæþþiġ（稳固的），即 stead（位置）＋ 形容词后缀 -y
column3: firmly fixed, or moving at an even rate without sudden change
column4: 稳的/稳步的/持续不变的
column5: Hold the ladder steady while I climb.|Sales showed steady growth all year.
column6: keeping the same position or pace throughout – 位置或速度全程不变
column7: 稳的：不摇不晃，位置守得住|稳步的：动是动，但速度不忽快忽慢|持续不变的：把这份不变拉长到整段时间

column2: 中古英语 steike ← 古诺尔斯语 steik（烤肉，指串在棍上烤的那块）
column3: a thick flat piece of meat or fish cut for grilling or frying
column5: He ordered his steak rare.|Grill the steaks for four minutes each side.
column6: a thick slab of meat cut to go on the fire – 切得厚、专拿去上火的一块肉
column7: 牛排：这种切法最常用于牛肉|肉排：同样切法用在别的肉上

column2: 中古英语 stelen ← 古英语 stelan（偷）← 原始日耳曼语 *stelaną（偷）；哥特语 stilan 与之同族
column3: to take something that belongs to another without permission
column5: Someone stole my bicycle from the yard.|He stole a glance at the clock.
column6: to take what is not yours while unseen – 趁人不见，把不属于自己的拿走
column7: 偷：擅自取走他人之物|窃取：取的多是无形之物，如资料或名声|暗中做：只取「不让人看见」这一面，如悄悄溜走

column2: 中古英语 steem ← 古英语 stēam（蒸汽、热气）← 原始日耳曼语 *staumaz（汽、气）← 原始印欧语 *dʰewh₂-（腾起、冒烟）
column3: the hot gas that water turns into when it boils
column5: Steam rose from the boiling kettle.|The mirror was covered in steam.
column6: water turned by heat into hot gas – 水受热化成的热气
column7: 蒸汽：水沸后化成的气|水汽：同是水化的气，更淡，可见为白雾|蒸：用这种热气把食物做熟这个做法

column2: 由 steam ＋ -er 构成；steam 一支 ← 古英语 stēam（蒸汽）← 原始日耳曼语 *staumaz（汽）
column3: a ship driven by steam power, or a pot that cooks food over boiling water
column5: The old steamer crossed the lake twice daily.|Cook the fish in a bamboo steamer.
column6: a thing that runs on steam or cooks by it – 靠蒸汽跑，或靠蒸汽把东西做熟
column7: 汽船：以蒸汽机为动力的船|蒸锅：靠水沸后的气把食物做熟的锅|蒸笼：同样靠气加热，只是编成一层层的笼

column2: 中古英语 stele ← 古英语 stīele ← 原始西日耳曼语 *stahlī（钢制之物）← 原始印欧语 *stak-（立定、坚固）
column3: a hard strong metal made from iron mixed with carbon
column5: The bridge is built of steel and concrete.|He steeled himself for bad news.
column6: iron worked hard enough to carry a great load – 把铁炼到能承重的硬度
column7: 钢：铁加碳炼硬后的那种金属|钢铁：连着铁一起说的通称，多用于工业|使坚强：把「炼硬」这层用到人心上

column2: 中古英语 steep ← 古英语 stēap（高的）← 原始日耳曼语 *staupaz ← 原始印欧语 *(s)tewp-（顶起、戳出）；「昂贵」义 1856 年始见于美国英语
column3: rising or falling sharply rather than gradually
column5: The path grew steep near the summit.|Prices rose at a steep rate.
column6: slanting so sharply that climbing it takes effort – 倾斜得厉害，要上去很费力
column7: 陡的：坡面立起来，不是缓缓抬升|急剧的：把陡坡的形状用在曲线上，涨落都快|过高的：价钱像坡一样立起来，故称高得离谱

column2: 中古英语 steeren ← 古英语 stēoran（掌舵、导航）← 原始日耳曼语 *stiurijaną（掌舵）
column3: to control the direction in which a vehicle or boat moves
column5: She steered the boat towards the shore.|He steered the talk away from money.
column6: to hold something on the course you want – 把行进的东西按住在你要的方向上
column7: 掌舵：手在舵上，本义即此|引导：把方向从船挪到话题或人身上|操控方向：强调不断微调、不让偏离

column2: 中古英语 stem ← 古英语 stemn（茎、干）← 原始日耳曼语 *stamniz（茎、树干）← 原始印欧语 *steh₂-（站立）
column3: the main upright part of a plant that supports leaves and flowers
column5: Cut the stem at an angle before watering.|Most complaints stem from poor service.
column6: the upright part that holds the rest up – 立着的那一段，别的都由它托住
column7: 茎：草木立着托住叶与花的那一段|柄：器物上供手握、也起支托作用的那一段|源于：把「由它长出」这层用到因果上

column2: 中古英语 steppen ← 古英语 steppan（迈步、行进）← 原始日耳曼语 *stapjaną（迈步）← 原始印欧语 *stebʰ-（支撑、踩踏）
column3: one movement of the foot in walking, or one level in a series
column5: He took a step back from the edge.|Follow these steps in order.
column6: one unit of advance from where you now are – 从当下位置往前推进的一个单位
column7: 一步：脚抬起落下走过的那一段|台阶：脚一次踏上去的那一级|步骤：把「一步」用到过程上，一次做一段

column2: 截自 stereophonic／stereoscope，词头 stereo- ← 希腊语 stereos（立体的、实心的）
column3: sound sent through two or more separate channels so that it seems to come from different places
column5: The album sounds better in stereo.|He bought a second-hand stereo.
column6: sound split across channels so it gains depth – 分成几路送出，听起来就有了纵深
column7: 立体声：左右分路播出、能听出方位的声音|立体声音响：播放这种声音的整套设备

column2: 中古英语 stern ← 古英语 styrne（严厉的、峻急的）← 原始日耳曼语 *sturnijaz（愤怒的、震惊的）← 原始印欧语 *ster-（硬、僵）
column3: serious and severe in manner, showing no willingness to bend
column4: 严厉的/严格的/不容商量的
column5: The judge gave him a stern warning.|Her stern look silenced the room.
column6: holding a hard line without softening – 板着不松口，不留通融的余地
column7: 严厉的：态度硬，声色不缓|严格的：把这份硬落到规矩上，一分不让|不容商量的：硬到连开口余地都不给（同形的「船尾」是另一支词，源自古诺尔斯语「掌舵」，与此无关）

column2: 中古英语 steward ← 古英语 stiġweard，由 stiġ（厅、屋）＋ weard（看守）合成，本义是看管家宅的人
column3: a person who looks after property or serves passengers on a ship or plane
column5: The steward brought blankets to the passengers.|He served as steward of the estate for years.
column6: one put in charge of looking after what belongs to another – 受托看管别人的产业或客人
column7: 乘务员：船机上照看乘客的人|管家：看管宅院与家产的人，本义在此|管理者：把「受托看管」抽出来，用于任何托管之事

column2: 中古英语 stikke（枝、棍）← 古英语 sticca（棍、枝）← 原始日耳曼语 *stikkô（棍、杆）← 原始印欧语 *(s)teyg-（刺、扎）；「粘住」义出自同根的 stician（刺入而留住）
column3: a thin piece of wood, or to become fixed to a surface
column5: He picked up a stick to draw in the sand.|The stamp would not stick to the envelope.
column6: a thin shaft, or the state of being lodged fast – 细长的一根，或扎住不动的状态
column7: 棍：削下或折下的细长一根|枝条：树上还没折下来的那种细长部分|粘住：从「扎进去就留在那儿」推来，指贴住不掉

column2: 由 stick ＋ -y 构成；stick 一支 ← 古英语 sticca（棍）与 stician（刺入而留住）← 原始印欧语 *(s)teyg-（刺、扎）
column3: tending to hold onto whatever it touches
column5: The table was sticky with spilt juice.|We are in a sticky situation.
column6: holding fast to whatever touches it – 碰上什么就抓住不放
column7: 黏的：触到就粘上，不易分开|难对付的：局面像黏上手一样脱不开身

column2: 中古英语 stif ← 古英语 stīf ← 原始日耳曼语 *stīfaz ← 原始印欧语 *steypós（硬、挺）；按常规演变本该读 /staɪf/，今读 /stɪf/ 或出自 stiffly 一类复合词中的元音缩短
column3: hard to bend or move out of shape
column4: 僵直的/不易弯折的/生硬的
column5: The new boots felt stiff at first.|His neck was stiff after the long drive.
column6: resisting any attempt to bend it – 想让它弯，它不肯
column7: 僵直的：关节或身体不肯屈|不易弯折的：材料本身抗弯|生硬的：把这份不肯通融用到举止与措辞上

column2: 借自拉丁语 stimulatus，是 stimulō（驱赶、用刺棒催）的完成被动分词 ← stimulus（刺棒）
column3: to make something more active or make someone more interested
column5: Coffee stimulates the nervous system.|The prize stimulated fresh interest in the field.
column6: a prod from outside that rouses something into action – 从外面戳一下，使对方活跃起来
column7: 刺激：外来的一戳，使反应起来|激发：把原本不显的兴致或潜力戳出来|促进：这一戳落在进程上，使推进得更快

column2: 中古英语 sting ← 古英语 sting（刺、扎出的伤）← 原始日耳曼语 *stingaz；动词一支 ← 古英语 stingan（刺）← 原始日耳曼语 *stinganą
column3: a sharp pain caused by a pointed part of an insect or plant piercing the skin
column5: A bee sting swelled up within minutes.|The cold wind stung his cheeks.
column6: a pointed jab that leaves a burning pain – 尖端扎一下，留下火辣的痛
column7: 刺：昆虫或植物身上那根尖端|刺痛：被扎后那种又尖又辣的痛感|蜇：把这一扎当动作说，多用于虫

column2: 中古英语 stiren ← 古英语 styrian（动、搅、扰）← 原始日耳曼语 *sturiz（骚动、喧扰）
column3: to move a liquid around with a spoon so its parts mix
column5: Stir the soup before you taste it.|His speech stirred the whole crowd.
column6: to set the parts of something moving so they mix – 让里面各部分动起来，混到一处
column7: 搅拌：用器具带着液体绕圈|搅匀：搅到各部分再分不出来|激起：把「使动起来」用到人心与情绪上

column2: 中古英语 stiche ← 古英语 stiċe（刺、扎，及扎出的痛）← 原始日耳曼语 *stikiz（刺、缝迹）← 原始印欧语 *(s)teyg-（刺、扎）
column3: one pass of a threaded needle through cloth
column5: The wound needed six stitches.|She sewed the hem with tiny stitches.
column6: one pass of the needle in and out again – 针进去再出来的这一趟
column7: 缝线：留在布上的那一道线迹|一针：针进出一次算一针，用作计量|缝合：把这些针连起来，把裂口合到一起

column2: 中古英语 stok ← 古英语 stocc（树干、木桩）← 原始日耳曼语 *stukkaz（树干）；「存货」义或出自刻记账目的对分木签（tally stick）之用法
column3: the goods a shop keeps on hand for sale
column5: The shop is out of stock until Monday.|He owns stock in three companies.
column6: the standing supply a business rests on – 一桩生意赖以立住的那批存底
column7: 存货：待售的那批货，如同支起铺面的那根干|股票：把公司的本钱分成份，持有一份就占一份|家畜：农家的活存底，同样是赖以立住的本
